answer: An agent economy can gate voting and high-value contracts behind a slowly earned, nontransferable reputation: peers attest to completed work, and a random audit checks a sample before credit is granted. One identity cannot simply copy another’s history, while fake identities must each do useful work and survive scrutiny to gain influence. The attacker therefore pays in compute, time, and labor for every credible persona; an ember of trust must be earned along the river of transactions, not minted like a lotus of fresh accounts.
